title: The Excuses of the Hypocrites • The Peace Proposal to Ghatafan • Single Combat • Safiyyah’s Courage • Sa‘d’s Wound • Nu‘aym’s Diplomacy

blocks.1: The longer the siege dragged on, the clearer the cracks inside became. The hypocrites and the weak in faith were looking for excuses to go back. Mu‘attib ibn Qushayr of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf had said, Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Kisra and Qaysar, yet today not one of us can even go to the toilet safely. Aws ibn Qayzi had said, O Messenger of Allah, our houses are exposed before the enemy; give us permission, let us go back.{{1}}
blocks.2: The Qur’an has put these words of the hypocrites like this,
blocks.4: And remember when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease were saying, what Allah and His Messenger promised us is nothing but deception. And when a group of them said, O people of Yathrib! There is no place for you here, so go back; and a party of them were asking the Prophet for permission (to go home), saying, our houses are exposed, whereas they were not exposed; rather, their intention was only to flee (by some means).{{1}}
blocks.5: An excuse that sounds beautiful on the tongue often hides only the wish to run from fear. The house is not exposed, the heart is exposed. The Qur’an has told their real condition like this,
blocks.7: If the enemies had entered upon them from all sides of Madinah and they had been asked to join the rebellion, they would surely have joined it, and would have stayed in their homes only a little.{{1}}
blocks.8: There was another group, of whom the Qur’an speaks like this,
blocks.10: (And that too) grudging toward you. So when danger comes, you will see them looking at you with eyes rolling, like one fainting from fear of death. Then when the danger passes, they lash you with sharp tongues out of greed for wealth. They never believed. So Allah has made their deeds worthless, and that is very easy for Allah.{{1}}
blocks.11: The same people, cowardly before the battle and greedy before the spoils; both are symptoms of the same disease, a deficit of faith. Set against this flight of the hypocrites, the Qur’an has stood up a measure, saying,
blocks.13: Indeed, in the Messenger there is for you an excellent example; for one who hopes in Allah and the Day of the Hereafter and remembers Allah much.{{1}}
blocks.14: For the one who looks for excuses, there are a thousand ways to flee. For the one who takes the Messenger as the example, there is only one way, forward.
blocks.16: The siege had gone on for nearly a month, and apart from the exchange of arrows there had been no major clash. When people were in pain from hardship, the Prophet {{1}} sent men to two leaders of Ghatafan, ‘Uyaynah ibn Hisn and al-Harith ibn ‘Awf, with a proposal: he would give one-third of Madinah’s dates, in return for their going back with their people. Talks moved forward, and a document was almost drawn up as well, though the final signing had not yet taken place.{{2}}
blocks.17: Before deciding, the Prophet {{1}} called the two Sa‘ds for consultation. They asked, is this a command from Allah, or your own decision? The Prophet {{2}} said, my own decision; seeing the Arabs pounce on you united, I thought I would break some of their strength. Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) said,
blocks.19: O Messenger of Allah, when we and these people were upon shirk, we did not know Allah; even then they could not eat a single date of ours for nothing, except through sale or as guests. Now that Allah has honoured us with Islam and given us dignity through you, are we to hand our wealth over to them? We have no need of this; by Allah, we will give them nothing but the sword, until Allah decides between us and them.{{1}}
blocks.20: The Prophet {{1}} said, then let it be your decision. Sa‘d (RA) took the document in his hand and erased it. Those who used to bow their heads in the Jahiliyyah, Islam had given those very same people the courage to say no with dignity. Not holding off the enemy with wealth, but fighting by the strength of faith.
blocks.22: Finding no way across the trench, a few horsemen of Quraysh chose a narrow spot, spurred their horses and leapt across to the other side of the Khandaq. ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wudd, ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb, Dirar ibn al-Khattab; four famous warriors came down onto the open ground between the trench and Mount Sal‘. ‘Amr was then one of the most famous warriors of Arabia; having been wounded at Badr he had not been able to take part at Uhud, and this was the first time he had returned to the field. He halted his horse and shouted, who will fight me? No one answered. ‘Ali (RA) stood up and said, O Messenger of Allah, I will. The Prophet {{1}} said, sit down, that is ‘Amr. ‘Amr said mockingly, did you not say that your dead go to Paradise? Then why do you not send even one against me? ‘Ali (RA) stood up again, and the Prophet {{2}} again said, sit down. The third time, when ‘Amr issued the same challenge, ‘Ali (RA) stood up again and said, O Messenger of Allah, I will go, even though he is ‘Amr. This time the Prophet {{3}} permitted. ‘Ali (RA) went close and first said, I call you to Allah, to His Messenger, to Islam. ‘Amr said, I have no need of that. ‘Ali (RA) said, then I call you to single combat.{{4}}
blocks.23: ‘Amr asked, who are you? He said, ‘Ali. ‘Amr said, the son of Abu Talib? He said, yes. ‘Amr said, cousin, among your uncles there are others older than you; I do not want to shed your blood. ‘Ali (RA) replied, by Allah, but I do want to shed yours.{{1}}
blocks.24: Unable to win in words, ‘Amr grew angry, got down from his horse, hamstrung it himself, then leapt at him. A fierce fight followed; ‘Amr struck ‘Ali (RA) on the head and wounded him, ‘Ali (RA) struck at his neck. So much dust rose that from outside one could not tell who had won. The Prophet {{1}} understood from the sound of takbir that ‘Ali (RA) had killed ‘Amr. The other three spurred their horses, crossed the trench and fled. When ‘Ali (RA) came back, ‘Umar (RA) asked, why did you not strip off his armour? There is no better armour in Arabia. ‘Ali (RA) said, when I struck, his private parts were exposed, so I felt ashamed to strip the clothes from the body of a cousin. Later Quraysh sent men wanting to buy ‘Amr’s corpse for a great sum. The Prophet {{2}} said, keep it, we do not eat the price of the dead.{{3}}
blocks.25: A single challenge, a single fight; the moment the greatest warrior of the ten-thousand-strong army was defeated, the rest understood that winning this siege was not going to be easy. Fear lifts only when someone steps forward.
blocks.27: The men able to fight were then in the trench. In the fortresses inside Madinah were the women and children, together with some men assigned to guard them. In Fari‘, the fortress of Hassan ibn Thabit (RA), was Safiyyah bint ‘Abd al-Muttalib (RA), paternal aunt of the Prophet {{1}}; Hassan (RA) was there too, on this very guard duty. A Jewish man began to wander around the fortress. Banu Qurayzah had by then broken the pact; the Prophet {{2}} and the Companions were facing the enemy, with no way to come back. Safiyyah (RA) said to Hassan (RA), this man may see the hidden side of the fortress, he may call more of his own people; go down and kill him. Hassan (RA) said, may Allah forgive you, daughter of ‘Abd al-Muttalib; you know well that this is not my work. Safiyyah (RA) herself took a stick in her hand and went down from the fortress, struck the man and killed him, then came back and said, go down, bring his belongings; only modesty stopped me, because he is a man. Hassan (RA) said, I have no need of his belongings.{{3}}
blocks.28: The men were in the trench then, the women alone in the fortress; yet one woman’s alertness and courage saved the women and children of the whole fortress. ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) was then a little boy, with the women and children in another fortress. ‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah (RA) was with him too; the two, each climbing on the other’s shoulders, would try to peep over the fortress wall to see how the fighting was going. ‘Abdullah (RA) saw that his father al-Zubayr (RA) was running now this way, now that; wherever there was danger, he was there. In the evening when his father returned, the son said, Father, I saw you today. Al-Zubayr (RA) said, you saw me, my son? Then may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.{{1}}
blocks.29: Even a child far from the battlefield had seen his father’s courage; that very sight perhaps later prepared him for the hardest fights of his own life.
blocks.31: ‘A’ishah (RA) was then in the fortress of Banu Harithah, and Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh’s (RA) mother was there too. One day Sa‘d (RA) was passing by the fortress in battle dress, the sleeves of his armour so short that his whole arm was bare, a spear in his hand, reciting in rhythm: wait a little, the time to see battle has come; when the hour of death comes, there is no harm in death. His mother called from behind, son, go quickly, you are late. ‘A’ishah (RA), seeing him, said, I wished Sa‘d’s armour had been a little longer.{{1}}
blocks.32: This very fear of the mother came true. ‘A’ishah (RA) used to say,
blocks.34: On the day of the Trench Sa‘d (RA) was wounded; a man of Quraysh struck him, who was called Hibban ibn al-‘Ariqah; the arrow pierced the vein of his arm. The Prophet {{1}} pitched a tent in the mosque, to look after him from close by.{{2}}
blocks.35: The arrow had pierced exactly that bare spot of the armour. The one who stands foremost with a weapon in hand is the first to bleed. The Prophet {{1}} kept him before his own eyes, so that there would be no lapse in care. Sa‘d (RA) had made du‘a, O Allah, if You have left any war with Quraysh remaining, keep me alive to fight them; and if this is the last war, make this very wound the occasion of my martyrdom, and do not give me death until my eyes are cooled concerning Banu Qurayzah.{{2}}
blocks.37: Nu‘aym ibn Mas‘ud of the Ghatafan tribe had accepted Islam in secret; his own tribe did not know. He came to the Prophet {{1}} and said, I have become Muslim, my tribe does not know; I will do whatever you say. The Prophet {{2}} said, you are only one man among us; if you can, create division among them, for war is the name of strategy.
blocks.40: Nu‘aym (RA) went first to Banu Qurayzah; in the days of the Jahiliyyah he had been their friend. He said, you know what my relation with you is. Quraysh and Ghatafan are not like you; this city is yours, your wealth, children and wives are all here, you have no way to move elsewhere. Their homes are elsewhere. If they get a chance they will take their gain, if not they will go back to their own land, leaving you alone to face this man; then you will not have the strength to hold him back. So do not enter the war with them without taking some of their leaders as hostages. Then he went to Quraysh and said to Abu Sufyan, the Jews regret their decision, they have sent word to Muhammad asking forgiveness; they have said they will hand over some of your leaders to be killed, and in return join him to finish off the rest. So if the Jews ask for hostages, do not give even one. He said the same thing when he went to Ghatafan too.{{1}}
blocks.41: On Saturday night Quraysh and Ghatafan told Banu Qurayzah, get ready, we will attack together. Banu Qurayzah replied, today is Saturday, we do not work; and we will not fight unless you give hostages. Quraysh and Ghatafan understood that Nu‘aym’s word was true; they refused to give hostages. Banu Qurayzah too understood that Nu‘aym’s word was true, that these people were merely opportunists; they too refused to fight alone.{{1}}
blocks.42: One man, saying three different things in three directions, broke the whole alliance without lying to anyone. Every word was true; only the time and place of speaking were calculated. Once the seed of suspicion is sown, an alliance no longer remains an alliance.

footnotes.6: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (the reply of Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA); Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) too was among those asking together). Sirah-based.
footnotes.7: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (the original/first narration, ‘Ali (RA)’s invitation and the proposal of single combat; in the dars it has been narrated combined with al-Bayhaqi’s second narration). Sirah-based.
footnotes.8: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wudd’s challenge and conversation with ‘Ali (RA); the first narration through Ibn Hisham, the second and detailed dialogue in al-Bayhaqi’s Dala’il al-Nubuwwah through Ibn Ishaq). Sirah-based; there are differences in detail between the two narrations, the main event is the same.
footnotes.9: Imam Ahmad ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), with the chain Nasr ibn Bab ← Hajjaj ← al-Hakam ← Miqsam); al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through the chain al-Thawri ← Ibn Abi Layla ← al-Hakam ← Miqsam, remarking ‘gharib’. In Musa ibn ‘Uqbah’s narration the name of the slain man is given as Nawfal ibn ‘Abdillah al-Makhzumi.
footnotes.10: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (the account of Safiyyah bint ‘Abd al-Muttalib (RA), through al-Bayhaqi, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr’s own narration). Sirah-based. ⚠ In some Sirah narrations cowardice is given as the reason for Hassan (RA)’s being among the women and children; Imam Ibn ‘Abd al-Barr and other muhaddithun rejected this narration as having a broken chain (munqati‘) and unacceptable. Imam al-Suhayli said, perhaps he was ill that day. The dars has not used this weak accusation, unjust to a Companion; he is shown on this very duty of guarding the women and children.
footnotes.11: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA)’s own narration, through Hisham ibn ‘Urwah from his father). Sirah-based.
footnotes.12: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (the narration of ‘A’ishah (RA), through Abu Layla ‘Abdullah ibn Sahl). Sirah-based.
footnotes.14: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Ghazwat al-Khandaq’ (Sa‘d (RA)’s du‘a, after being wounded). Sirah-based.
footnotes.15: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Ghazwat al-Khandaq’ (the instruction of the Prophet {{1}}, within the account of Nu‘aym (RA)). The words ‘al-harbu khud‘ah’ (war is strategy) themselves also occur in Sahih al-Bukhari 3030 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA)), but there in a different context; the connection of this sentence with Nu‘aym’s event is Sirah-based.
footnotes.16: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Ghazwat al-Khandaq’ (Nu‘aym ibn Mas‘ud (RA)’s whole diplomatic campaign, separate messages to the three parties). Sirah-based.
footnotes.17: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Ghazwat al-Khandaq’ (the events of Saturday night, the mutual suspicion of both sides). Sirah-based.

quiz.q: What was Mu‘attib ibn Qushayr essentially complaining about?
o: The extreme lack of food
The weak and short-sighted leadership of the army
The promised treasures of Kisra and Qaysar
A wrong war strategy

quiz.q: What did Aws ibn Qayzi say when asking permission to go back?
o: That he was feeling ill
That there was trouble in the family
That he did not have enough weapons
That the houses were exposed before the enemy
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir; Surah al-Ahzab 33:13.

quiz.q: Why did the Qur’an call the hypocrites’ excuse ‘our houses are exposed’ a lie?
o: The houses were really protected, they only wanted to flee
Because they really had no houses at all
Because they knew there would be no war
Because the Prophet ﷺ had not given permission

quiz.q: Cowardly before battle, greedy before the spoils: this behaviour is a sign of what?
o: A sign of mere lack of courage
A sign of a deficit of faith
A sign of the effect of poverty
A sign of lack of training
quiz.e: In the light of Surah al-Ahzab 33:19.

quiz.q: What can be applied from the hypocrites’ beautiful-sounding excuses?
o: It should be assumed that every excuse given by everyone is true
Giving excuses is never a fault
One should sit in judgment on others’ excuses
One should check the real reason behind each of one’s own excuses

quiz.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ want to give Ghatafan in return for peace?
o: Half of Madinah’s land
Some camels and horses
The release of all prisoners of war
One-third of Madinah’s dates

quiz.q: Why did Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) reject the peace proposal?
o: Because the Prophet ﷺ had forbidden him
Because Ghatafan themselves finally withdrew the whole proposal altogether
Because the time for writing the document had run out
They gave nothing free even in the Jahiliyyah, let alone after Islam

quiz.q: What can be learned about self-respect from Sa‘d’s (RA) rejection?
o: Everything should be given up to keep the enemy happy
After receiving honour, one should not bow the head easily
The leader’s decision should not be questioned
All problems can be solved with wealth

quiz.q: Who stood up against ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wudd in single combat?
o: ‘Ali (RA)
‘Umar (RA)
al-Zubayr (RA)
Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)

quiz.q: After how many times of ‘Amr’s challenge did the Prophet ﷺ permit ‘Ali (RA)?
o: The first time
The third time
The second time
The fourth time

quiz.q: What reason did ‘Ali (RA) give for not taking ‘Amr’s armour?
o: There was no time in the haste of battle
The armour had been torn and ruined by the blow
He felt ashamed because the private parts had been exposed
The Prophet ﷺ had forbidden it

quiz.q: When Quraysh wanted to buy ‘Amr’s corpse, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: They fixed a price for it
The corpse will not be returned
First agreed, then refused
We do not eat the price of the dead

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell ‘Ali (RA) to sit down the first two times?
o: Because he had little trust in ‘Ali
He wanted to give someone else a chance
Considering ‘Amr’s strength and fame
Because the time had not yet come

quiz.q: Why did ‘Amr’s defeat become a great blow to the whole allied army?
o: Because he was their only soldier
A food crisis arose with his sudden death
Quraysh stopped the war at once
Because he was their most famous warrior

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ refuse to take money in exchange for ‘Amr’s corpse?
o: Because taking the price of the dead is against honour
Because the amount of money was small
Because on principle he did not want any dealings with Quraysh
Because ‘Ali (RA) forbade it

quiz.q: What can be learned from ‘Ali (RA) stepping forward even though everyone was silent?
o: One person’s courage can change the whole situation
Stepping forward alone is always a dangerous act
Nothing should be done without the group’s consent
One should not advance without the leader’s permission

quiz.q: What can be learned from ‘Ali’s (RA) sense of shame even at the moment of victory?
o: Respect should not be shown to the enemy
Modesty should not be given up even after victory
When one wins a war, taking everything is natural
For kinship’s sake everything must be given up

quiz.q: Who killed the Jewish man who was wandering around Hassan’s fortress?
o: Safiyyah bint ‘Abd al-Muttalib (RA)
‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA)
Hassan ibn Thabit (RA)
‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah (RA)

quiz.q: Why did Safiyyah (RA) not bring down the man’s belongings herself?
o: There was no time to go down
Only out of modesty, because he was a man
She did not dare go down alone
Hassan (RA) forbade her

quiz.q: Why is Safiyyah’s incident important, when the men were all in the trench?
o: It was a rare exception
Even one woman’s alertness can save a whole fortress
Because she was the Prophet’s ﷺ paternal aunt
Merely to prove Hassan’s personal weakness

quiz.q: What can be learned about alertness from Safiyyah’s incident?
o: One should always depend on others in everything
There is no need to think about the defence of women
On seeing danger one can take action oneself
One should attack at the slightest suspicion

quiz.q: What can be learned about child-rearing from the incident of Ibn al-Zubayr seeing his father?
o: Children should always be kept near war
It is improper to question a father’s work
A child should not be praised
An example of good conduct shapes the child

quiz.q: Who shot Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) with the arrow?
o: Abu Sufyan himself
‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl
Hibban ibn al-‘Ariqah
‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wudd

quiz.q: Why did ‘A’ishah (RA) say she wished Sa‘d’s armour were longer?
o: Because she did not like war
Because Sa‘d himself had requested it
Because she saw danger in the arm left bare by the short sleeves
It was merely a general remark about the beauty of the armour

quiz.q: What can be learned from Sa‘d’s du‘a (if I live I will fight, if not, martyrdom)?
o: One can remain content with Allah’s decision in both situations
Wishing for death is always the greatest and best act
Life has no meaning without war
There is no need to make du‘a when wounded

quiz.q: Why did Nu‘aym’s strategy succeed, although he did not lie?
o: He used weapons
Both sides were already weak
He supposedly bribed both sides separately with plenty of money
By telling the truth at exactly the right time and place he sowed suspicion

quiz.q: What can be learned about conflict resolution from Nu‘aym’s strategy?
o: No talk with the enemy should ever have been held then
Even the truth, said in the right place, can reduce disorder
Strategy means lying
One man cannot change a big situation
